original_checklist_items.text: Delete the 10 duplicate copies before re-importing — runbook `migrations/2026-08-24_repair-delete-duplicates.sql` (inspect → backup → soft-delete + **null the fingerprint**, which is what makes the re-import work per BUD-32 → verify). Keeps the earliest insert of each group; $42.08 of expenses removed, so Debit Card - NEO reads that much too low until corrected via the app's reconciliation flow (owner accepted the temporary drift). One pair (Touch Prepaid $17.04, two hashes in one batch) needs checking against the July statement first — may be a real double payment. Must precede BUD-36. _(blocker - S)_

Heal the historic imports by re-importing month by month, oldest first — 157 Debit Card rows carry no fingerprint (they get **stamped** on match) and 152 carry the dead v1 formula (they get **re-keyed**, BUD-34/37). No SQL backfill: the diagnostic proved every stored hash is v1 and therefore unreproducible, so there is nothing to verify a reconstruction against, and the import path repairs both classes on its own. Order: run `migrations/2026-08-24_statement-import-rekey-action.sql` → clear the 10 duplicate copies (BUD-39; the FX rows STAY — see BUD-40) → re-import ONE month and confirm the receipt reads created 0 / matched N / re-fingerprinted M → repeat per month → finish with a full-year upload that must create nothing. _(blocker - M)_

(ASTRA M-01 reconciliation) Verify the already-implemented deleted-hash recognition and restore choice before the owner import day; reconcile now includes deleted exact-hash rows. Preserve fingerprint semantics until the current restore/re-import witness identifies a remaining defect. → [Verified delta](<ASTRA/Budget — ASTRA Book.md>) _(friction - S)_

(ASTRA-BUD-4) ERA actuals share canonical account type, currency, ownership and custom-period semantics; blocks trusted E-04/E-08 money summaries. → [Execution sheet](<ASTRA/Budget — ASTRA Packets.md>) _(blocker - M)_

Inspect current owner DB contracts; split by domain before implementation. → [Restore evidence](<ASTRA/Budget — ASTRA Book.md>) _(friction - M)_

Merchant-match → Voice Draft Transactions — when a spoken message contains a known merchant, run it through `matchMerchantMapping()` so the draft pre-selects Category/Subcategory from the merchant map (on top of existing NLP category matching). → `src/lib/nlp/` + drafts review UI _(annoyance - M)_

Reconcile-only ("audit") mode for statement import — a run that matches parsed rows against already-logged transactions and **creates nothing**: no `create` entries, no balance deltas, no merchant learning writes, only a verdict per row. The matcher (`/api/statement-import/reconcile`) is already balance-neutral; what's missing is a session mode that stops before commit and a result surface that reads as a report instead of a work queue. Mode must be chosen at upload and be visible on the review screen, so an audit run can never be mistaken for an insert run. → `src/features/statement-import/sessionModel.ts` + `src/app/statement-import/page.tsx` _(friction - M)_

Trip-aware matching — the current matcher is single-account, single-currency, −7/+1 days, tolerance `max($1, 10%)` (`AMOUNT_TOLERANCE_MIN`/`_PCT`), which is right for Lebanon and wrong abroad on three counts: (1) **FX** — the bank posts a converted amount in the card's currency while the manual log is in the trip currency, so raw amount comparison fails outright; compare via an **implied rate** (`statement_amount / logged_amount`) clustered across the trip, accept rows near the cluster median and flag the outliers, instead of widening the flat tolerance; (2) **posting lag** — foreign settlement plus weekends routinely exceeds 7 days, so the window needs a trip profile; (3) **account scope** — candidates are hard-filtered to the statement's `account_id`, but trip spend may be logged against the trip account created by `activate_trip` (in the trip's currency), so the candidate pool must span the card account **and** the trip's account. → `src/lib/statement-reconcile.ts` _(friction - L)_

Reconciliation exception report — the output of an audit run, ranked, in **both** directions: statement rows with no logged transaction (a tap never logged) and logged transactions with no statement row (double-logged, cash-not-card, or not yet posted). Lead with the arithmetic that triggers the whole exercise — total statement vs total logged for the period, with the gap stated in one number — then the ranked exceptions, `probable`/`ambiguous` pairs first with a one-tap confirm/reject that resolves the pair without inserting anything. Small gaps within tolerance close silently; a large gap (owner's threshold ~$100) is the alert. → `src/components/statement-import/` _(friction - M)_

Claude has no OS boundary on native Windows at all; its declared control is the harness-level `canUseTool` allowlist, which screens tool calls and not what a permitted tool's subprocess then does, and nothing about it has been observed. **Security consequence:** any job could read `.env`, `~/.codex/auth.json`, `~/.claude` credentials and the supervisor's own store — so `admitProfile()` refuses both profiles and every `deliver` ends at `profile-not-admitted`. Context & Agent Model §4: "profile ineligible for confidential/unattended work". **Two obvious fixes were checked and are not fixes:** a per-path `deny` list in the Codex permission profile only hides the canary (the read surface stays the whole host, so it would game the fixture rather than close the hole), and relocating the supervisor store does nothing because the canary's store was *already* outside the workspace and was read anyway. **Proposed direction:** an OS boundary applied from outside the SDK — the elevated Windows sandbox backend (its invocation did not return within 120 s non-interactively and needs investigating), a low-privilege local account whose ACLs deny the host profile, WSL2, or a container.
